machine: arm64 macOS, R 4.5.0 / tinygrad venv py3.10 (numpy 2.2.6), torch 0.17 / libtorch

method.note: tinygrad times are the best of 3 runs inside one process (JIT compiled once); pytorch single-process numbers are quoted because its --repeats path clones the input inside the timer and inflates both time and RSS

remeasured_after: Gram-Schmidt buffer fix in TESTING/nipals_tinygrad.py: on this tinygrad version .assign() is a no-op when applied to an indexed view, so Gram-Schmidt had silently been skipped and the later components were contaminated by earlier ones. Timings barely change (the projection is O(nvar x k) per iteration); accuracy and iterations below are post-fix.
caveats: Metal has no fp64: tinygrad runs float32, so tol=1e-6 sits at the rounding floor and its stopping test is noisier than fp64 (F2000 complete: 448 vs 386 total iterations); eigenvalues still agree with the fp64 reference to ~2e-5 relative over ten components.
Block size barely changes wall time at any tested shape; unrolling 8 steps costs ~1.2-1.8x redundant iterations but saves per-op dispatch.
The CPU device only works when clang resolves to Apple's toolchain; the anaconda wrapper shadows it on PATH and via CC.
Run-to-run spread is +/-20 percent; the F2000 tier favours pytorch because kernel-launch latency dominates.
